text: That evening, in the gathering darkness: Holmes has scruples about taking Watson to-night
why: ¶196 places Holmes's scruples about taking Watson 'to-night' at dusk, in the gathering darkness, after Roylott has driven off that evening.

text: What is the danger that Holmes expects to-night?
why: A plain question; Holmes has just said there is 'a distinct element of danger' and the story has given reasons to wonder what it is.

text: What is the danger that Holmes expects to-night? — whatever reached Julia in that room
id: q.what_danger=whatever reached Julia in that room
why: Julia died in this room, Holmes has said the cause was probably 'some more tangible cause', and Helen's account of the whistle and the bed-room makes it a possibility the reader has reason to consider. The label does not claim to know what it was.

text: What is the danger that Holmes expects to-night? — Dr. Roylott's strength and temper, if he finds them there
id: q.what_danger=Dr. Roylott's strength and temper, if he finds them there
why: Roylott's violence, immense strength, the blacksmith incident, the bent poker, and his threat to Holmes all make him a reasonable candidate for the danger.

text: What is the danger that Holmes expects to-night? — the cheetah and the baboon loose on the grounds
id: q.what_danger=the cheetah and the baboon loose on the grounds
why: ¶27 says the cheetah and baboon 'wander freely over his grounds' and are feared, so their being loose is a possibility the story has given reason to consider.

text: What is the danger that Holmes expects to-night? — the gipsies in the plantation
why: The gipsies camp in the plantation (¶27, ¶61–62), and Helen and Holmes have both raised them as possible sources of the whistle and the 'band'.
